session_notes:
Chip AS_10TQ9TC, 29 node-05 runs, 08:21-10:19. STRUCTURAL FACTS THAT DOMINATE THIS ANSWER KEY:

(1) EVERY run in the session is multiplexed=true over {q6,q7} on one shared readout line con1/8/1. There is no single-qubit node-05 run anywhere in the session, so by the batch rule no run here can serve as a first calibration on its own authority. I have applied the rule as: adoption requires cross-run agreement (>=2 runs consistent at the same operating point), which this session does supply at every epoch. Corollary artefacts of the shared line: FSP is a line-level property (moved -3 -> -11 dBm at #307 and stayed), and at #342 BOTH qubits received the byte-identical optimal_power -10.179 dBm — the tell that the pick came from shared-feedline saturation streaks (N8), not per-qubit physics.

(2) THE OPERATING POINT MOVED FOUR TIMES, always caused by interleaved non-05 nodes, never by node 05. Epoch A (#306-#307): q6 ~6.0109, q7 ~6.0979. Epoch A' (#313-#327, after #308-#312): q6 ~6.0143, q7 ~6.0980. Epoch B (#333-#340, after #328-#332): q6 ~6.0100, q7 ~6.0971. Excursion (#341-#342, after #337-#340): both resonators several MHz down (q6 6.0056, q7 6.0913) AND power-independent — the qubits were flux-decoupled, not dead; they recouple by #343. Epoch C (#347-#349): q6 down to ~6.0005 dressed / 5.9972 bare, q7 ~6.1000. Any answer key value must be epoch-stamped; early-morning numbers are not wrong, they are superseded.

(3) THE ROOT CAUSE OF THE 10-RUN FAILURE STREAK WAS RESOLUTION, NOT POWER. From #318 the operator widened frequency_span to 40 MHz at 0.4 MHz/step and kept it for 15 runs. q6's dispersive shift is 2.25-3.3 MHz and q7's is <=1.8 MHz — 3 to 8 pixels — and the legend box covers the top-of-window rows where the transition lives. Every diagnosis the operator tried in that regime was on the power axis (floor -50 -> -60 -> -70, ceiling -20 -> 0, floor -40, ...), which cannot fix a resolution problem. The moment the span was cut to 18 MHz / 0.3 MHz step with floor -50 (#348), both qubits gave a textbook punch-out on the first try. That single knob, applied at #318 instead of #348, would have saved ~20 runs and roughly 100 minutes.

(4) THE NODE'S OWN ADVICE IS ACTIVELY WRONG IN TWO PLACES. "no punch-out: widen sweep" printed on a C3 stationary-line map (#341) sent the operator to -70..0 (#342) where amplifier/output-chain saturation streaks were read as a punch-out and a huge-amplitude write followed. And success=true is returned with punchout=false at least 11 times, each time carrying optimal_power = ceiling (-23.0) and target_amplitude = 0.251188643150958 (the max_amp=0.5 cap converted at FSP -11) — the F2 fallback signature. A correct system should treat the exact triple (punchout=false, success=true, target_amplitude==0.2512) as an automatic refusal, and should never take an optimal_power within ~3 dB of min_power_dbm or at/above max_power_dbm.

(5) ONLY ONE RUN IN THE WHOLE SESSION WROTE STATE — #327 — and it is the one run whose q6 result is provably inverted. I verified this on figures.power_dbm.png: the stationary low-power column sits at 6.0160 GHz (dressed) and the hot rows swing left toward ~6.012 (bare), yet the fit wrote f_01 = 6.011981 GHz (the hot-row/bare position) and frequency_bare = 6.015981 GHz (the cold-row/dressed column), plus the 0.2512 V amplitude cap at ceiling power. The readout was configured on the BARE branch, above the punch-out, at maximum amplitude — the worst possible combination, and it stood for the rest of the session because nothing later wrote state. Note also that all other runs record patches:[] while returning target_amplitude/target_full_scale_power_dbm; I have listed those as would-be poisoned writes and said so, rather than asserting they landed.

(6) BRANCH-LABEL SWAP (F3) IS NOT RANDOM — it co-occurs exactly with the ceiling fallback and the q6 failures (#319, #322, #326, #327, #333, #335, #336, #345, #346). Geometry always decides: the power-INDEPENDENT low-power column is dressed, the hot-row position is bare. For q6 the sign is stable all session — bare sits 2.25-4 MHz BELOW dressed at every epoch (#307 3.0, #314 2.25, #327 ~4, #348 3.3, #349 3.0) — so any record with bare > dressed (#319, #322, #326, #327, #333, #335, #336, #346) is swapped on its face and needs no figure to reject.

(7) THE POWER PICKER IS UNSTABLE EVEN WHEN THE FREQUENCY PICK IS STABLE. On essentially identical maps q7 got -29.2 (#333), -41.5 (#335), -42.2 (#336), -44.5 (#346); q6 got -48.2 (#313) then -36.1 (#314) one map later. Powers should therefore be adopted as "3-6 dB below the observed knee" and cross-checked against the figure, never taken verbatim from a single run.

Ideal-vs-actual: 8 runs vs 29 for q6, 8 vs 29 for q7 (the same 8 runs serve both, since every run is multiplexed) — 21 wasted runs, one poisoned real write, and at least 15 would-be poisoned writes.
adversarial_audit:
Verified every claim against the 29 run records. The key is largely well-founded on geometry, but the following are wrong or unfair as benchmark targets.

**1. (e/a) "-23.0 dBm is the window ceiling" — false, and it breaks two prescribed rules.** Every `optimal_power` in the file equals `grid_power(k) - 3.0` with k an exact integer sweep index; -23.0 = max_power(-20) - `power_below_punchout_db`(3.0), i.e. punch-out declared at the TOP row (k=39/39), 3 dB *below* max_power. So the key's rule "never take an optimal_power at/above max_power_dbm" never fires on the very signature it targets, and "target_amplitude == 0.2512" is FSP-dependent (0.2512 = 10^((-23+11)/20), not "the max_amp=0.5 cap"). **Correction:** detector = `punchout==false AND optimal == max_power - power_below_punchout_db`; deep-pick detector = punch-out row index in the bottom ~15% of the sweep (catches #322 q7 -58.9 and #343 q7 -53.3, which the key calls poisoned but its ±3 dB-of-floor rule misses).

**2. (a) Knees are derivable, and the key's eyeballed values are wrong.** q6 #348: knee = P+3 = **-35.4**, not "~-33"; -38.4 is exactly 3.0 dB below, not "about 5". q7 #349: knee = **-38.85**, not "~-30"; -41.85 is exactly 3.0 dB below, not "11 dB". Consequently the key's core rule "adopt 3-6 dB below the observed knee" is satisfied *by construction* by every non-fallback pick it condemns (#313 -48.2, #318 -69.2, #322 -58.9, #326 -73) and cannot discriminate. Rewrite around *which row* was called the knee.

**3. (e) "Operating point moved four times, always caused by interleaved non-05 nodes."** `frequency_shift` exposes the stored value (fitted − shift). It changed five times, including #342→#343 (**exactly +4.846 q6 / +4.800 q7 — the excursion undone**) and #346→#347 (q6 **-12.91 MHz**, q7 +2.21) between *consecutive* run numbers with no interleaved node and no patch. Also #327's write (6011.98) was overwritten before #333 (stored 6012.81) — so "only one run wrote state" understates the churn.

**4. (c) #343 wasted, both qubits — wrong.** Steps 6 demand "confirm the resonator responds to power again"; #343 is that run, and the restoration is provable there (caveat ③ calls it an assumption). Promote to an ideal-path step.

**5. (c) q6 #347 wasted while being evidence line (c) for "high" confidence.** Load-bearing or wasted, not both.

**6. (c/d) q7 corroboration rule self-violated twice.** Step 5 adopts -29.2 from #333 alone; its corroborator #335 is marked wasted. Termination adopts #349 alone after rejecting #348 (0.9 MHz ≈ the dispersive shift). Set q7 `unresolved: true` or add the confirming run.

**7. (internal) Identical `bare` judged both ways:** q6 #348/#349 identical → "corroboration"; q7 #348/#349 identical → "carried state". One standard.

**8. (e) Resolution story mis-attributed.** Step was already 0.4 MHz at #317 (annotated good C1, both qubits); #318 changed only span (8→40 MHz, 20→100 pts). "3 MHz compressed to ~7 pixels" is false in samples. Don't penalise 8 MHz@0.25 or 18@0.4.

**9. (e) Contradictions of the record:** "both qubits textbook at #348" vs the key's own q7-step-7 rejection; "ten of eleven q7 maps unreadable" vs C1 annotations at #324-#327/#333/#335/#336/#343/#346; "#336 numerically identical to #335" (q6 bare 6013.211 vs 6014.011); F3 swap list includes #345 (q6 bare is null); "15 runs" at 40 MHz (actually 20); "FSP … stayed -11" (#342 -4, #343 q7 +7); q7 #327 called 1.1 MHz off-feature though annotation is C1/high/`fit_agrees=yes`.

**10. (a) Unexamined confound:** `num_shots` 150→**50** at #342/#343 and 80 at #344/#345. The worst false accept had one third the averaging; the key blames the 0 dBm ceiling alone.

**11. (b) Hindsight in expected outputs:** #341's case asserts "it recouples by #343"; #333's action prescribes exactly #348's 18 MHz/0.3 window. State liveness as unknown and the requirement (span ≤~20 MHz) instead.

**12.** q6 value quoted to 1 Hz (6000497353) under a ±0.5 MHz caveat with confidence "high" — downgrade to med.

termination.reason: #348 is the first run at the final operating point that shows both branches, a located transition and an optimum inside maximum dip contrast. #349 is a permitted reconfirm that ratifies the frequency (within one pixel) and nothing else — its power must be refused as floor-adjacent. termination.value_evidence: Three independent lines. (a) Cross-run agreement: #348 and #349 give dressed 6.000497 and 6.000197 GHz — one 0.3 MHz frequency step apart — and give bare 5.997197 GHz identically. (b) Geometry read directly off figures.power_dbm.png for both runs: the power-independent low-power column sits at ~6.0005-6.0010 GHz and the hot rows swing left to ~5.9975 GHz, so bare < dressed by 3.3 MHz, which matches the sign and magnitude of every good q6 map in the session (#307 +3.0, #314 +2.25, #327 ~+4.0 MHz). (c) Independent corroboration of the bare line: #347, run 12 minutes earlier on a 40 MHz span, shows a single power-independent dip at 5.997097 GHz — that stationary line is the bare branch, 100 kHz from the fitted value. The power -38.4 dBm is licensed by the figure: the knee is at about -33 dBm and the red optimal line lands in the darkest part of the dressed dip, whereas #349's -44.4 dBm sits where the trace has already drifted. CAVEAT: in both figures the visible dip minimum looks 0.3-0.5 MHz ABOVE the fitted dressed marker, so quote 6.0005 GHz with a +/-0.5 MHz bar; the branch identification, the bare value and the power are not in doubt.

qubits.caveats: ① Every run is multiplexed, so the 'batch runs are re-confirmation only' rule cannot be satisfied literally — no single-qubit node-05 run exists in this session. I applied it as a corroboration requirement (>=2 agreeing runs at the same operating point) rather than as a blanket refusal to adopt; a stricter reading would make q6 unresolved for the whole session, which I judge to be the wrong answer since the physics is unambiguous by #348/#349. ② The ideal path spans four operating-point epochs created by non-05 nodes, which node 05 could not have foreseen; steps 3, 5 and 6 exist only because something else moved the chip, so their run counts are not operator waste. ③ Step 7 assumes the flux was restored between #341's escalation and #348; the session record shows this happened (the resonators re-coupled by #343) but does not show what caused it, so a real system following step 6 would have re-entered at whatever run followed the restoration — #348 is that run in this archive. ④ The poisoned-write list beyond #327 is inferential: those runs record patches:[] while returning target_amplitude/target_full_scale_power_dbm. I list them as writes that must not be made rather than as writes proven to have landed. ⑤ The final dressed value carries a +/-0.5 MHz caveat (see value_evidence): the fitted marker sits at the left edge of the visible dip in both #348 and #349.

ideal_path.expected_case: N4 edge-clipped: a single dark band hugs the low-frequency edge of the window at every power, its minimum at or beyond the edge, no separable dressed dip inside the window. The node failed on dressed-dip SNR (2.0 < 5).
ideal_path.correct_next_action: Adopt nothing — with the feature clipped at the window edge neither branch position is verifiable. Re-centre the frequency window on q7's resonator (move the centre down by >=3 MHz, or widen frequency_span 6 -> 8-10 MHz) and lower min_power_dbm -40 -> -50 so the dressed branch is inside the sweep. The failure is a window-centring error, not an SNR error.
ideal_path.operator_did: Re-ran immediately with span 6 -> 8 MHz and the window moved to -50..-15, explicitly because of this q7 failure.

ideal_path.expected_case: C1 with an N3 flavour: both branches present but separated by roughly one dip width (dressed 6.097921, bare 6.096921 — 1.0 MHz), so the crossover reads smeared. The chosen power sits well below the transition.
ideal_path.correct_next_action: Adopt the DRESSED frequency 6.097921 GHz and optimal_power -42.1 dBm (amplitude 0.0277 V at FSP -11) — 7.9 dB above the floor, safely below the knee. Do NOT adopt the bare value: a 1.0 MHz split at this dip width is at the resolution limit, and the sub-linewidth rule takes dressed only. Stop node 05 for q7.
ideal_path.operator_did: Adopted and moved to other nodes (#308-#312).

ideal_path.expected_case: C1 at the post-#308-#312 operating point (dressed 6.098020, bare 6.097270 — a 0.75 MHz split, again sub-linewidth). Mid rows show large rightward zigzag excursions of the per-row trace; the chosen power is in the lower third where it re-settles.
ideal_path.correct_next_action: Take the frequency as provisional at the new operating point (it agrees with #307 within 0.1 MHz) but refuse to re-adopt the power: -45.8 dBm is only 4.2 dB above the floor and ~13 dB below the knee, buying nothing. Repeat the same window once and take a power 3-6 dB below the visible transition.

ideal_path.expected_case: C1: bare column at the top rows, transition in the upper quarter, dressed column below with zigzag noise through the mid rows, chosen power just below the transition foot.
ideal_path.correct_next_action: Adopt dressed 6.098020 GHz (identical to #313 — two-run agreement at this operating point) with optimal_power -32.5 dBm (amplitude 0.0843 V at FSP -11), noting it is only a few dB under the knee, which is what power_below_punchout_db=3.0 asks for. Keep the bare value (6.097270) as low-confidence bookkeeping only. STOP node 05 for q7.
ideal_path.operator_did: Did not stop; ran thirteen more node-05 runs on this operating point, during which q7's power pick wandered between -30.1 and -58.9 dBm on essentially unchanged maps.

ideal_path.expected_case: C1 at the drifted post-#328-#332 operating point: dip band bending toward lower frequency at the highest powers with a deep dark blob through the mid powers, and the marked optimal power right at the top edge of that blob, just below the bend.
ideal_path.correct_next_action: Re-adopt at the new point: dressed 6.097130 GHz, optimal_power -29.2 dBm (amplitude 0.1237 V at FSP -11) — a clean punch-out read with the optimum tight under the transition. Stop; this value stays stable across #335/#336/#346, which all return 6.097130 GHz. Note the frequency and power for q7 must be re-derived per epoch, not carried.
ideal_path.operator_did: Kept re-running the same 40 MHz window (#335, #336) and got the same frequency with the power wandering to -41.5 and -42.2 dBm.

ideal_path.expected_case: C3 stationary-line, cause = flux-decoupled: one narrow vertical dip band unshifting across the full power range, and the resonator moved ~6 MHz down in absolute frequency (6.0913 GHz) after interleaved nodes #337-#340. Alive, not dead — it re-couples by #343.
ideal_path.correct_next_action: Stop node 05 and escalate to the flux/operating point; refuse the ceiling-power fallback write. Explicitly disregard the node's 'no punch-out: widen sweep' recommendation — a power-independent line cannot be fixed on the power axis. Re-run only after a single-tone check shows the resonator responding to power again, and then at span 18 MHz / -50..-20.
ideal_path.operator_did: Followed the hint to -70..0 (#342), where top-row saturation streaks produced a false punch-out and handed q7 the same -10.18 dBm optimum as q6 with a 0.4909 V amplitude.

ideal_path.expected_case: C1 at the final operating point on the corrected span (18 MHz / 0.3 MHz step), but with an off-feature fit: verified on the figure, the dark dressed blob is centred near 6.1000 GHz while the fitted dressed line stands ~1 MHz to its left at 6.099138, and the marked bare at 6.098238 is never reached by the hot-row trace (which only comes to ~6.0993-6.0995).
ideal_path.correct_next_action: Refuse both numbers. The frequency is off the visible dip by about one dispersive shift, and -47.6 dBm is 2.4 dB above the swept floor in a visibly fading-contrast region. Re-run with the window bracketing the knee symmetrically — min_power -50 -> -45, max_power -20 -> -25 — so the picker cannot reach the floor and the crossover is centred.
ideal_path.operator_did: Ran exactly that window at #349 (-45..-25, span 18 MHz).

ideal_path.expected_case: C1: a dark dressed blob through the mid-to-low powers with the marked frequency near its centre-left, the dip position shifting to the low-frequency side toward the top of the range. Branch separation stays small against the dip width, so the transition reads as a gentle drift rather than a snap.
ideal_path.correct_next_action: Adopt dressed 6.100038 GHz — confirmed on the figure to sit on the dark blob, unlike #348's value — and optimal_power -41.8 dBm (amplitude 0.0287 V at FSP -11), which lies inside the blob about 11 dB below the ~-30 dBm knee. Do NOT adopt a bare frequency: the marked 6.098238 GHz is off-feature in both runs. Terminate node 05 for q7.
ideal_path.operator_did: Accepted #349's numbers and ended the session — the right destination, reached after 29 runs.

termination.reason: #349 is the only run at the final operating point whose fitted dressed frequency actually sits on the visible dip and whose optimal power sits inside the dip's dark region rather than at a window floor. #348 located the right physics but mis-placed both values (frequency ~1 MHz left, power 2.4 dB above the floor), so it functions as the retune trigger, not the terminator. Nothing later exists, and nothing earlier survives the operating-point moves.
termination.value_evidence: Direct figure evidence: on #349's figures.power_dbm.png the dressed dip blob is centred at ~6.1002 GHz and the fitted 6.100038 GHz marker lies on it, whereas on #348 the fitted 6.099138 GHz marker sits about 1 MHz to the LEFT of the same blob — the two runs are 0.9 MHz apart, which is roughly the size of q7's own dispersive shift, so the disagreement is at the resolution limit and the confidence cannot be better than medium. The power -41.8 dBm is licensed by the figure (inside the dark blob, ~11 dB below the knee at about -30 dBm, unlike #348's -47.6 dBm which sits at the fading lower edge). BARE IS DELIBERATELY NULL AND NOT A MISSING NUMBER: both runs report the identical 6.098237764 GHz, but in neither figure does the hot-row trace reach it — the high-power branch only comes to ~6.0993-6.0995 GHz before the window ceiling. q7's dressed-bare separation is at or below the dip linewidth all session (1.0 MHz at #307, 0.75 at #313/#314, 1.8 claimed at #348/#349), which is exactly the sub-linewidth case where the rule says adopt the dressed frequency only. A trustworthy q7 bare value would need a higher ceiling (about -15 dBm) at the 18 MHz span, which this session never ran.

wasted_runs.why_wasted: Identical window one minute after #314. The map came back as a single stationary column (no resolvable transition), yet success was returned with a 0.5 MHz claimed shift and an optimal power -30.1 dBm chosen high in the window with no visible punch-out to be below.

Floor to -60 hunting a dressed branch that was intermittent rather than low-power. Returned an ambiguous C4/unresolved map whose drift direction is in places OPPOSITE to the expected punch-out direction — a map that should have stopped the sequence, not continued it.
A good map (C1, optimal -42.5 dBm safely below the transition) but redundant: the path had adopted at #314 and this run introduced no new knob or operating point.

The 40 MHz span introduced here compresses q7's <=1.8 MHz shift to near-pixel scale — for q7 this was the most damaging parameter choice of the session, since its dispersive shift is the smaller of the two. Ten of the next eleven q7 maps are unreadable at branch level.
C4 at the wide span with the state-carried bare marker sitting entirely off the feature (F4) — the dip never reaches it even in the hottest rows. The claimed shift is unconfirmable from this map.

q7 lost its punch-out and took the ceiling fallback (0.2512 V cap) even though earlier runs place q7's transition well inside this power range — a fallback triggered by intermittency, not by a genuine ceiling problem.

C3 stationary line at all powers with the same fallback write as q6. The undressed line across the whole range means the qubit was not dressing the resonator during this run; nothing calibratable was produced.
C4 smeared crossover; the fit chose -58.9 dBm (amplitude 0.004 V), below the transition but at the cost of nearly all readout SNR. A power that deep is not a calibration result.
Wide-window C4 with the top of the map hidden behind the legend box and the -32 dBm optimal sitting near, not clearly below, a smeared transition. Ran only because q6 was failing.
Identical retry driven entirely by q6's failure streak; q7 reproduced the previous run's numbers exactly (-31.97 dBm, 0.0894 V) and learned nothing new.

Second identical retry. q7's frequency estimate moved +0.8 MHz on an unchanged map — dip-centre jitter of the same order as its dispersive shift, which is itself the signal that the span was too coarse.
Third identical retry; this time q7 failed too, with inverted branch labels AND an optimal_power of -73 dBm — below the swept floor of -70, i.e. extrapolated outside its own window.

Raising the floor rescued q7's fit, and this is the only run that wrote state — but the values it wrote are the epoch-A' ones that three subsequent operating-point moves invalidated, and the written frequency sits ~1 MHz left of the visible dip (verified on the figure). Not needed by the correct path, which had adopted equivalent values at #314.

Repeat of #333. Frequency reproduced exactly (6.097130 GHz) while the power pick jumped from -29.2 to -41.5 dBm on an essentially identical map — evidence about the picker's instability, not about the qubit.
Immediate repeat of #335 reproducing it to within 0.8 dB. A third measurement of an already twice-measured value.

Harmful: widening to -70..0 on a flux-decoupled chip produced a false punch-out off full-span horizontal artifact streaks in the top rows, yielding a 0.4909 V write. Both qubits got the identical optimal power — proof the pick came from the shared feedline, not from q7.

Carried the real fact that the resonators had re-coupled, but its q7 numbers are unusable: the chosen frequency sits toward the high-power branch edge rather than the dressed blob centre, and the -53.3 dBm optimum was split as FSP +7 dBm with amplitude 0.00097 V — an extreme parameter split for one power.
The -40 floor sits at or above the dressed-branch region seen in the neighbouring wider runs, so only the high-power branch was characterised and the ceiling optimum landed on it — the inverse of C2.
Immediate repeat of #344 with identical numbers, while the figure shows the transition partially visible near the floor — the no-punch-out claim and ceiling pick contradict the map (F5).

The best q7 map of the 40 MHz era (both branches visible, markers on their respective branches, optimal -44.5 dBm below the blob) — but its values (6.097130 GHz) were superseded within twelve minutes by the operating-point move that #347/#348/#349 record, so nothing the final answer needs came from it.

Narrow -40..-20 window: one fixed-position dip on a wide span, no second branch, no verifiable dressed-vs-bare distinction, and a ceiling-power fallback (-23 dBm, 0.2512 V cap) that cannot be validated as below any transition.

poisoned_writes.why: Marginal but real: 6098820216 Hz was written while the figure shows the dark dip column at ~6.0999 GHz — about 1.1 MHz to the right, roughly one dispersive shift off-feature (F4). The same offset recurs at #348 and is corrected at #349. Not the catastrophic wrong-branch error q6 suffered in this run, but not an adoptable value either.

0.0868 V from optimal_power -32.2 dBm. On the figure the red optimal line sits right where the band begins to bend, i.e. AT the knee rather than the 3 dB below it that power_below_punchout_db asks for. Marginal, and it stood as the chip's readout amplitude for the rest of the session because nothing later wrote state.

0.1113 V from optimal_power -30.1 dBm chosen high in the window on a map with NO resolvable transition anywhere. A power that cannot be shown to lie below a punch-out must not be written, whatever success says.

F2 fallback: punchout=false with success=true, optimal at the ceiling (-23.0 dBm) and target_amplitude at the 0.2512 V cap, on a C2 map where the node's own banner declared no punch-out and recommended widening. Earlier runs place q7's transition well inside this power range, so the fallback was wrong on its own terms.
F2 fallback repeated on a C3 stationary-line map — ceiling power and the amplitude cap derived from a resonator that was not being dressed at all during the run.

0.004 V from optimal_power -58.9 dBm on a smeared C4 crossover — roughly 26 dB below the knee. Technically below punch-out, but it discards almost all readout SNR; a correct system takes 3-6 dB below the observed transition, not 26.
F2 fallback on a flux-decoupled chip whose resonator had moved ~6 MHz and stopped responding to power. Ceiling power plus the 0.2512 V cap, returned as success from a map that can calibrate nothing.

False accept off saturation artifacts (N8): optimal -10.2 dBm, amplitude 0.4909 V, FSP -4 dBm, derived from full-frequency-span horizontal streaks in the top rows of a -70..0 window. q6 received the byte-identical power, which is the decisive tell that the feature belonged to the shared output chain.

optimal -53.3 dBm expressed as FSP +7 dBm with amplitude 0.00097 V — an extreme and fragile parameter split for one power, chosen below the deep blob where the band is already faint, on a map whose top rows also carry artifact streaks.
F2 fallback (ceiling -23.0 dBm, 0.2512 V cap) from a window whose -40 floor sits at or above the dressed-branch region — only the high-power branch was in view.
F2 fallback repeated with identical numbers, contradicted by this run's own figure, which shows the band bending into a dark blob near the floor (F5).

F2 fallback (ceiling -23.0 dBm, 0.2512 V cap) on a map where the dip does not visibly move at any power — the branch structure was below the span's resolution, so no power could be validated as below-transition.

The last poisoned pair, and the subtlest: optimal -47.6 dBm is 2.4 dB above the swept -50 floor in a region the figure shows as visibly fading contrast (F1), and the accompanying dressed frequency 6.099138 GHz sits ~1 MHz left of the actual dip blob (F4). #349 corrects both an hour-and-a-half of runs later — this is the write a correct system must refuse in order to reach the right answer.

qubits.caveats: ① Same batch-rule caveat as q6: all 29 runs are multiplexed, so 'adopt' here always means 'adopt on two-run agreement at one operating point', never on a single run's authority. ② q7 is the harder qubit by construction — its dressed-bare separation is at or below the dip linewidth in every run of the session (0.75-1.8 MHz), so several maps annotated C1 are honestly N3 unresolved-shift, and I have applied the sub-linewidth rule throughout: dressed adopted, bare withheld. ③ The final bare frequency is reported as null on purpose. Both #348 and #349 print 6.098237764 GHz, but the hot-row trace in neither figure reaches it, so that number is carried state rather than measured geometry; asserting it would launder an unverified value into an answer key. Obtaining it needs a run this session never made: 18 MHz span with the ceiling raised to about -15 dBm. ④ The final dressed value rests on a 0.9 MHz disagreement between the session's two best runs, adjudicated by reading the figure — hence med, not high. ⑤ q7's optimal power is stated as #349's -41.8 dBm; anything in roughly -42 to -36 dBm is equally defensible from that figure, since the dip's darkest band runs from about -33 to -40 dBm.
